directAnswer: You can check a web server by using command line tools like `ping`, `curl`, or `telnet` to test connectivity and response.
summary: This guide provides methods to verify the status and performance of a web server using various tools.

sections.heading: Checking Connectivity
sections.body: Use the `ping` command to check if the server is reachable. This sends packets to the server and measures response time.

sections.heading: Testing HTTP Response
sections.body: Use `curl` to send a request to the server and check the HTTP status code. A successful response will typically return a status code of 200.

sections.heading: Using Telnet
sections.body: Telnet can be used to check if a specific port (like 80 for HTTP or 443 for HTTPS) is open on the server.

steps.title: Ping the Server
steps.detail: Open your command line interface and type `ping [server_address]`. Replace [server_address] with the actual IP or domain name.

steps.title: Check HTTP Response with Curl
steps.detail: In the command line, type `curl -I [server_address]`. This will return the HTTP headers including the status code.

steps.title: Test Port with Telnet
steps.detail: Type `telnet [server_address] [port]` in the command line. For example, `telnet example.com 80` to check if port 80 is open.

faqs.question: What does a status code of 404 mean?
faqs.answer: A 404 status code indicates that the server could not find the requested resource.

faqs.question: How can I check if my server is down?
faqs.answer: If you cannot ping the server or receive a response from `curl`, it may be down or unreachable.

faqs.question: What should I do if my server is not responding?
faqs.answer: Check your network connection, verify the server address, and ensure the server is powered on and configured correctly.

caveats: Firewall settings may block ping or telnet requests, leading to false negatives.
Different operating systems may have variations in command availability and syntax.
